title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Auditorium on 1969-01-17
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A raw but excellent soundboard capture—marred by a clanky bass‑drum pedal—but saved by a blistering Dark Star, monster Other One and other epic jams.
ai_review.review: The recording is a vintage sound‑board tape with minimal hiss for its era; the only technical blemish is an overly loud bass‑drum pedal that some listeners find distracting. Musically the show is electric, featuring a scorching Dark Star, a ferocious Other One and tight, soaring jams through Cryptical Envelopment, St. Stephen, The Eleven and Death Don't Have No Mercy. Overall the performance’s high energy outweighs the recording quirk.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4‑5 stars and praise the musical peaks; recording issues are noted but not enough to outweigh the strong performance, yielding a weighted average around 4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear vintage sound‑board tape with minimal hiss; however the bass‑drum pedal is excessively loud and clanky, causing distraction for some listeners.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A powerful first set builds into a marathon second set of extended jams; transitions (e.g., Cryptical→Other One) feel seamless and the climax hits with Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven → Death Don't Have No Mercy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as fierce with one of Garcia's most ferocious solos; his solo in Love Light is noted but the track suffers a splice.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass highlighted throughout—both praised for its presence and criticized when it overpowers due to pedal issues; some reviewers note Phil’s “tree‑trunk” pick style on The Other One.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey's bass drum pedal is a recurring complaint (clanky, overly loud), though the overall drumming is praised.
